title: Reports emerge of a 28-point US-Russia peace plan for Ukraine
body:
On 19 November 2025, Foreign Policy reported, citing Axios, that the United States and Russia had worked secretly on a 28-point peace plan for Ukraine. According to the reports, the plan covered four areas: ending the war in Ukraine, security guarantees, European security, and the future of US relations with Kyiv and Moscow. Foreign Policy noted that it might have been inspired by President Donald Trump's 20-point plan for Gaza.

US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Kirill Dmitriev, Vladimir Putin's envoy and head of Russia's sovereign wealth fund, reportedly negotiated it in Miami over three days in late October. Witkoff also discussed the plan with Rustem Umerov, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's national security adviser, in Miami. Politico reported that the Trump administration hoped for a deal within days, possibly in the week of 19 November.

Dmitriev said Russia's position was being heard and sounded optimistic. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia's stance had not changed and that there was nothing to add to the talks in Anchorage. It was unclear whether Kyiv or European allies supported the plan. Zelensky said Kyiv had received some "positions and signals" from Washington, and Ukraine insisted on a seat at the negotiating table.

Foreign Policy said peace talks had stalled since the August summit in Alaska. A planned October summit in Budapest had collapsed, and the United States had recently sanctioned Rosneft and Lukoil.
